subject: Renewal: Stability Accelerator + Burst Credits
messages:
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>
To: Lina Morales <lina@avacloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Stability Accelerator + Burst Credits

Hi Lina,

As we approach your June 30 renewal, I wanted to outline a proposal to address the latency tail and traffic spikes you flagged in last quarter's review. Based on usage patterns and your peak-day traces, we recommend: 

- Stability Accelerator: guaranteed 99th-percentile latency window of 120ms for the production route (applies to hosted inference).
- Burst Credits: 1 month of burst capacity (equivalent to 2x committed throughput) for onboarding new features without provisioning additional reserved capacity.
- 10% committed capacity increase year-over-year (optional) with discounted token rates for the incremental commit.

I attached a short SLA amendment draft and a capacity summary. If this package looks right, we can fold the SLA addendum into the renewal and route it to procurement for signature.

Request: can we schedule a 30-min sync this week to walk through the amendment and confirm the effective date? Available windows: Wed 11am-1pm PT, Thu 2pm-4pm PT.

Thanks,
Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0192
---
Attachments: redwood-sla-amendment-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 48KB), capacity-commitment-summary.xlsx (XLSX, 26KB)

From: Lina Morales <lina@avacloud.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ava Cloud Procurement <procurement@avacloud.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal: Stability Accelerator + Burst Credits

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifying points from our side before we sync with procurement: 

1) For the Stability Accelerator, does the 99th percentile window apply across regions or only the primary US cluster? We need guarantees for cross-region failover.
2) For Burst Credits, can those be used across both hosted and dedicated capacity? We have a rollout in August that may temporarily run heavier inference on hosted.
3) Our procurement team will need to see the exact SLA language around crediting and remediation steps (credits vs. rollback vs. penalty).

Procurement is looped in. Procurement lead is Tom B. at procurement@avacloud.com — he prefers DocuSign for redlines.

We can take the meeting Thu 2pm PT. Lina

Lina Morales
Head of Platform, Ava Cloud

Subject: Re: Renewal: Stability Accelerator + Burst Credits

Hi Lina / Tom,

Thanks — confirmed for Thu 2pm PT. Quick answers ahead of the call so procurement has context: 

- Stability Accelerator: the 99th percentile SLO will be scoped to the region(s) you specify on the amendment. Default is US-primary; we can add EU as an explicit region with a separate measurement bucket and remediation thresholds.
- Burst Credits: they are transferable between hosted and dedicated routes so long as the model variant and resource class match; credits are consumed on a first-match basis. We can add guardrails that prevent burst usage from overflowing your dedicated pool without explicit approval.
- Remedies: draft defines crediting (percentage of monthly invoice based on minutes breach), operational remediation (priority routing, on-call escalation), and an executive SLA review for repeated breaches.

Attached is a slightly revised SLA amendment that includes region scoping placeholders and the initial remedies language. I've also added an operational runbook appendix that describes failover routing and how burst credits are applied.

If procurement is comfortable with DocuSign, we can prepare a version for signature after we confirm region scoping during the call.

Cheers,
Rohan

Rohan — quick internal notes after Thu's call (keeping short): 

- Procurement is focused on measurable remedies and a clean DocuSign flow; avoid open-ended credits language.
- They asked for an effective date that aligns with their billing cycle: July 1 preferred (they close books on the 30th).
- Recommended concession: 1 month of burst credits + 5% uplift on committed capacity at renewal, priced at our internal upsell margin. We'll propose the uplift as optional with a sweetened incremental token rate.
- Ops: Evelyn to confirm cross-region measurement feasibility and how runbook triggers map to the SLA.

Next steps: finalize amendment with region fields filled (US + EU), create DocuSign packet, and prepare a short procurement cover note.

Ben

We reviewed the SLA amendment and procurement has a couple of small redlines around the credit calculation and an explicit clause limiting burst credits to production traffic only. Procurement confirms they're comfortable with a July 1 effective date, contingent on DocuSign flow and a single executive sign-off.

2) Can you confirm the EU measurement window will be enabled on Day 1 of the amendment (we need parallel monitoring).
